methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Daylight Computer is a Series A-stage consumer technology company founded by Anjan Katta. The company has raised $10M to date. The analysis covers a single applicable valuation method, as no public or private comparable companies are available in the comp universe for this sector.

The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression. Using the $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying the multiplier yields an implied valuation of $20M. This approach assumes that the company's current capitalization reflects investor risk assessment at Series A entry, and that progression to the next financing round would command a standard multiple on that base.

The triangulated valuation range is $17M to $23M, with a median of $20M. The lower bound reflects downside scenarios within the stage-progression framework; the upper bound reflects upside scenarios. Given the absence of public or private comparables and reliance on a single methodology, key uncertainties include: whether the $10M raised proxy accurately represents fair value at entry, whether standard Series A to Series B multipliers (2.0x) apply to this specific subsector, and whether the company's capital efficiency and traction warrant positioning at the high or low end of the range. Additional data on revenue, unit economics, or peer benchmarks would materially improve precision.
